chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Dance reassures him about his excited manner
summary: Thompson worries he sounds too excited on tape; Dance tells him commitment is good.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I think too as we go on, and as your career develops, this will become evident too. You know, the places that you play and the people that you play with and the reaction and your going abroad, and that sort of thing, it'll come out, don't you think so?

I think so. And I just happened to realize something else that I thought about when I was listening to myself talk. I told you that I'm so excited about this taping that we're doing, and I find that even I notice in my voice that I've been very exciting sounding, excitable, you know. And I had made up my mind last night when we finished our session that I was going to come down a little bit, and see if I couldn't be more factual with my talking and kind of be a little more nonchalant. Because this is very exciting to me, as I said, and talking about my early life and the interests I have in this music, and your kindness to interview me has probably gotten me high pitched.

Well, I don't agree with you. I think that when you feel stirred up and committed and interested, that it comes through. And I think it's catching to the listener. I think it's a question of commitment, and commitment is always a very, very good thing.

I think what many people are lacking, and they are lacking in commitment. So I wouldn't restrain myself in any way, I would go -- I would just speak from your heart, as you have been, and I think we had a wonderful taping session yesterday and I would relax and just speak on as it comes to you. I think it was very satisfactory yesterday, I wouldn't make any change.
